reasoning_content:
Excellent. tex2pdf-service is fully functional with working API. Now let me verify remaining services coverage and count. Let me list backend directories vs built images.

Backend dirs: 28 (berichtskonfigurator, decision-log-store-service, demos-einwendungsmanagement, demospipes, demosplan, dokumentenaufbereitung-data-service, dokumentenaufbereitung-monorepo, dokumentenpruefung, dokumentenschwaerzung-orchestrator, dokumentenschwaerzung-pdf-pii-detector, dokumentensuche, fristenmanagement, graph-api, ki-guv-ai-testing, ki-guv-explainability, ki-guv-feedback, kommentar-service, nachforderungen, ner-extraction, norm-matching, rechtsquellenvorbereitung, request-proxy, risikohinweis-service, subsumtion-service, tatbestandsmerkmalsextraction, tex2pdf-service, xoev-adapter = 27). Plus 03-shared-services ki-validierung.

Images built: 27 backend + ki-validierung + 2 base + 2 addon = 32. demosplan and tatbestandsmerkmalsextraction not built (no Dockerfiles).

Let me verify ki-validierung image and confirm demosplan has no Dockerfile. Also check what demosplan contains.

Let me do a comprehensive sweep. Also test fristenmanagement and dokumentenpruefung more. Let me quickly attempt a couple more services with env to see how many start.

Actually the key question is whether the installation is "complete and operational according to the guide". Given the guide requires external runtime deps not installed, the assessment is nuanced. Let me gather broad evidence: try starting the set of services that don't strictly require external deps and see which become HTTP-ready.

Let me do a batch run of several services and probe.

Let me be efficient - run several at once with unique ports.

action.command:
cd /workspace && cat > /tmp/probe.sh <<'EOF'
declare -A S=(
 [fristenmanagement]=1
 [berichtskonfigurator]=2
 [risikohinweis-service]=3
 [decision-log-store-service]=4
 [ki-guv-feedback]=5
 [ki-guv-ai-testing]=6
 [graph-api]=7
 [xoev-adapter]=8
 [dokumentensuche]=9
 [kommentar-service]=10
)
for svc in "${!S[@]}"; do
  n=${S[$svc]}
  docker rm -f pb-$svc >/dev/null 2>&1
  docker run -d --name pb-$svc -p $((19000+n)):8000 $svc:latest >/dev/null 2>&1
done
sleep 25
for svc in "${!S[@]}"; do
  n=${S[$svc]}
  st=$(docker inspect --format '{{.State.Status}}/{{.State.ExitCode}}' pb-$svc 2>/dev/null)
  code=$(curl -s -m 4 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:$((19000+n))/docs 2>/dev/null)
  printf "%-30s state=%-14s /docs=%s\n" "$svc" "$st" "$code"
done
EOF
bash /tmp/probe.sh
